title: DelaunayTri
summary: Create a legacy 2-D Delaunay triangulation object.

gpu_support.notes: `DelaunayTri` builds host topology using a combinatorial geometry algorithm. GPU-resident numeric inputs are gathered at the constructor boundary; there is no runmat-accelerate kernel because the result is object topology rather than an elementwise or reduction tensor.

description: `DelaunayTri` creates the legacy MATLAB triangulation object shape for 2-D point inputs. RunMat stores both legacy properties (`X`, `Triangulation`, `Constraints`) and modern triangulation-compatible aliases (`Points`, `ConnectivityList`) so downstream helpers such as `triplot`, `freeBoundary`, `nearestNeighbor`, and `pointLocation` can consume the same object.
behaviors: `DelaunayTri()` returns an empty 2-D triangulation object with 0-by-2 points and 0-by-3 connectivity.
`DelaunayTri(X)` accepts an N-by-2 finite point matrix and constructs one-based triangle connectivity.
Duplicate point coordinates are ignored for triangulation while the public point matrix preserves the supplied rows.
Nonempty constrained triangulation inputs and 3-D point forms return explicit unsupported-target errors rather than placeholder topology.

examples.description: Create a 2-D triangulation from a point matrix
Create from coordinate vectors and plot the mesh

faqs.question: Does RunMat support constrained or 3-D DelaunayTri inputs?
faqs.answer: Not yet. Those forms fail deterministically with `RunMat:DelaunayTri:Unsupported`.

faqs.question: Does DelaunayTri preserve gpuArray residency?
faqs.answer: No. The constructor gathers numeric inputs because triangulation creates CPU object topology and not a dense numeric GPU result.
